newsitem.title: AZERBAIJAN: IBRD to increase lending to Azerbaijan from 1998.
newsitem.headline: IBRD to increase lending to Azerbaijan from 1998.

text.p: The World Bank plans to increase credits to Azerbaijan from 1998, its resident representative said on Thursday.
"If the annual credit limit for Azerbaijan was previously $30-40 million, we will double it to $80 million from next year," Tefik Yaprak told a news conference.
He said the main reasons for the decision were an improvement in major macroeconomic indicators and the fact that the Azeri government was following correct economic policies.
Yaprak said the first tranche of a $70 million Structural Adjustment Credit (SAC) would be transferred to the National Bank's account in two weeks.
The World Bank approved a $70 million SAC with an annual interest rate of 0.75 at the end of July.

"Another tranche of this loan will be allocated to the republic once the conditions of boosting banking sector reform, totally liberalising domestic and foreign trade and improving state social policy have been met," Yaprak said.
He also said privatisation should speed up. "The Azeri government has achieved big positive changes in this direction, but the reform should be continued," he said.
The World Bank has lent $270 million to Azerbaijan since 1992.
